# Possession labelling for BAR-ATH — technical document

*More than a Hack 2027, Phase 1. Team: [team name, members]. Repository: [public URL].*
*Submission: `candidate_v14.csv` (199,319 rows), MD5 `5e7363fc83c6f56a923033894a28d3a1`, regenerated by
`python src/make_submission.py` (section 10).*

## 1. Summary

Every frame is labelled by a two-part probabilistic model and a duration-aware decoder:

1. **Dead ball (D vs alive)** comes from interpretable evidence on the provided data: player tempo, the ball's
   position and movement, and cues from the aligned broadcast recording (replays and close-ups are almost always dead
   time).
2. **Team in possession (H vs A)** comes from a gradient-boosted classifier on team-level tracking features. It is
   trained only on open data: the 7 IDSSE / DFL Bundesliga matches and the 3 Metrica Sports sample games. Their clean
   tracking is first degraded by a simulator so that it looks like Metrica's automatic single-camera tracking: ball
   dropouts, smooth position noise, aerial-ball parallax and fragmented player tracks. Its probability is averaged in
   equal parts with that of a bidirectional GRU trained by a team member on open DFL and PFF data (section 3.3).
3. **A Viterbi decoder per half** combines both, with switch penalties, minimum durations and a soft minimum
   possession length. That length prior is what keeps the number of possessions realistic, which the ranking metric
   (spellF1) rewards.
4. **A short-possession verifier** takes a second look at the decoder's short decisions. A wrong-team flip that the
   decoder suppressed is inserted, and a decoded possession shorter than 4 s is handed to the other team, only when a
   classifier trained on the external sets is confident (section 3.5). Its evidence is identity-free tracking cues, the
   blended team probability's margins and the bidirectional GRU's own margin.

The provided match was never used to choose between model versions from round 6 onwards. Model choices were made on
held-out external matches (section 6). On those, the submitted model reaches spellF1 0.77–0.83 with its own dead-ball
estimate and 0.79–0.89 with the true dead ball on the two full-pitch sets (section 7).

## 2. Assets used and dropped

| Asset | Use |
|---|---|
| Tactical ATD (players, ball) | Main input. Own parser; `video_frame = frame_id - 1`; speed channel is m/s. |
| Tactical homography | Read by the feature builder (camera centre), but not used by the submitted model's evidence (the ATD is already in pitch coordinates). |
| Broadcast recording: ATD + homography | Aligned to the tactical timeline by a constant lag per half, found by matching ball positions: tactical = broadcast + 4,014 frames (1st half), + 26,920 (2nd half); the lag is constant to ±1–2 frames in every 2-minute block. Used for (a) dead-ball cues: no valid homography means a replay, close-up or crowd shot; (b) filling gaps in the tactical ball track where the broadcast shows live play that agrees with the tactical tracking. |
| Smart Tagging | Evaluated as team and restart evidence; its phase team agreed less with the reference than our own model, so it is not used. |
| Tactical video (images) | Not used in the submission. Ball detection on the wide tactical view (pretrained WASB, a YOLO fine-tuned on tracking pseudo-labels) did not reach a useful quality, and a perfect ball track is worth < +0.02 in simulation. |
| Tactical video audio | A referee-whistle detector was built (template from the kick-off whistles) but is **not** used in the submission: its only support was the 5-minute public window. |
| Broadcast audio / video | Investigated (commentary speech recognition, camera framing); neither helped on external validation, so neither is used. |
| Open data | IDSSE / DFL (Bassek et al. 2025, CC BY 4.0) and Metrica Sports sample data: training. PFF FC / Gradient Sports FIFA World Cup 2022 tracking (provider's access form): training of the bidirectional GRU. SkillCorner open data (MIT): evaluation only. |

## 3. Method

### 3.1 Features of the provided match

Per frame: positions of all tracked players with their team (no identities), the ball where seen (the tactical ATD
ball, gaps filled from the aligned broadcast ball), nearest-player distances per team, players within fixed radii,
ball speed and stillness, ball beyond a line, time since the ball was last seen, broadcast-view validity and live
agreement. All team features are computed for both teams symmetrically, so the classifier sees "own side vs other
side" and is trained with a side swap.

### 3.2 Dead-ball evidence

An aliveness log-odds `a` per frame is the sum of capped terms:

- mean player speed over ±1 s and ±3 s, looked up 1.5 s ahead (players react to the referee late);
- ball more than 0.5 m beyond a line;
- ball unseen for more than 1 s;
- ball still (moved < 0.6 m over ±0.5 s);
- ball moving fast (> 5 m/s) inside the pitch;
- broadcast without a valid homography (replay, close-up, crowd shot);
- broadcast showing live play that agrees with the tactical ball.

Frames between the end of the first half's grading window and the second kick-off are forced dead. These rules
were written on day one while checking them against the public window (see section 6). Two learned dead-ball models
trained on open data were later evaluated but not adopted.

### 3.3 Team-in-possession model

- **Labels.**
  - DFL: the per-frame BallPossession flag of the open data.
  - Metrica: built from the frame-synchronised events, read as *controlled* possession. The team is that of the last
    controlling event (set piece, pass, carry, recovery, shot, ball lost). Challenges, ball-out and fouls received do
    not change possession. A spell that follows the other team's spell counts as a change only if the new team shows
    control inside it: a completed pass or shot, or the ball kept for at least 1 s. Otherwise it is merged back into
    the previous team's possession. This mirrors the challenge definition: a touch without control, a deflection, or
    an aerial duel without subsequent control is not a change.
- **Simulated automatic tracking.**
  - Clean open tracking is degraded with `sim.V3`. The ball goes missing in long runs, more while the ball is dead
    and around stoppages, at rates calibrated to aggregate statistics of the provided tracking (no labels involved).
  - Position noise is low-passed: players 0.15 m, ball 0.35 m.
  - Aerial balls are projected to the ground through a high side camera, and player tracks are fragmented.
  - An adversarial-validation check against the provided tracking caught and removed an earlier version whose
    per-frame noise doubled all speeds.
- **Features.**
  - Nearest-player geometry, players within radii and a pressure-aware control score per team.
  - Own-half occupancy, set-piece formation, team shape and team movement.
  - Ball-free short-horizon team interactions: change of each team's spread (a team that wins the ball spreads out),
    speed of the last defensive line, reversal of the team centroid's direction, pressing velocity towards the
    nearest opponent, and supporting runs.
- **Model.**
  - LightGBM binary classifier: 400 rounds, learning rate 0.05, 63 leaves, min 200 samples per leaf, feature fraction
    0.8, bagging 0.7, L2 1.0. Deterministic mode, fixed seed, 8 threads; every 2nd frame is used for training.
  - Training data: 7 DFL matches (weight 1 each) and the 3 Metrica games, each in 3 degradations (weight 2 per game).
- **Blend with a sequence model.** The classifier's probability is averaged in equal parts with that of a
  bidirectional GRU (`models/bigru_dfl_pff_v1`: 64 units, dropout 0.15, 11 epochs, three seeds averaged) trained by a
  team member on the open DFL matches (their own possession flag) and on PFF World Cup 2022 tracking, with the same
  kind of degraded team-level inputs. The GRU alone is weaker than the classifier on DFL and Metrica, but the blend is
  better than either on most external contexts. The weight 0.5 was chosen from a grid fixed in advance (0.25 / 0.5 /
  0.75) by the worst-case regret over the external contexts (section 6).
- **Smoothing.** The blended probability's logits are averaged over ±25 frames (±1 s).

### 3.4 Decoding

Per half, a Viterbi decoder over {H, A, D} uses the emission scores S[H] = a/2 + log p, S[A] = a/2 + log(1 − p) and
S[D] = −a/2, where p is the smoothed probability that home has the ball. Log-probabilities are ≤ 0, so a confident
team call gives no bonus to "alive" over "dead". The decoder also uses:

- a switch penalty of 12 between H and A, and 30 between alive and dead;
- minimum durations of 8 frames for a possession and 50 frames for a dead-ball stretch;
- a soft minimum possession length: ending a possession after d < 175 frames costs an extra 48 · (1 − d/175).

The soft length prior was the largest single decoder gain. It discourages one-second flickers without forbidding
genuinely short possessions.

### 3.5 Short-possession verifier

Possessions shorter than 4 s are 18–33% of the true possessions in the external sets but carry 36–47% of the lost
spellF1 credit. The team probability does point to the right team on most frames of 71–84% of them, but brief
wrong-team flips (≥ 0.5 s) inside long possessions are just as frequent (1.0–1.6 per alive minute against 0.8–1.7 true
short possessions), so the length prior has to suppress short changes; loosening it loses on DFL and Metrica. The
verifier therefore re-examines two kinds of candidates taken from the decoded output itself:

- *insert*: runs of ≥ 12 frames inside a decoded possession where the smoothed probability favours the other team;
- *delete*: decoded possessions shorter than 4 s.

Over the candidate interval only, it computes: ball visibility, speed and in-flight share; which team's players are
nearest to the ball and how close they get; touches detected by each team; distinct players of the candidate team
holding the ball and the longest hold; contested share; depth towards the candidate team's attack and distance to the
touchline; the change of each team's centroid speed (transition reaction); the time since the last decoded restart;
the lengths of the enclosing or neighbouring decoded possessions; the blended team probability's margin (smoothed and
raw); and the margin of the BiGRU alone (its three checkpoints averaged). Two LightGBM classifiers, one per candidate
type (`models/short_verifier_{ins,del}_g_blend50.txt`), are trained on the blend's candidates in the external sets
(DFL with the tracking-derived controlled labels, Metrica with the event-derived controlled labels, SkillCorner
phases). On DFL, whose matches all trained the shipped BiGRU, the BiGRU probabilities come from leave-one-match-out
copies of it (same recipe, retrained without that match), so that the classifiers learn from margins of a network
that never saw the match, as on BAR-ATH. A candidate is positive when at least half of its frames belong to the
candidate team and a true possession of that team overlaps it with IoU ≥ 0.3.

An insertion needs p ≥ 0.65 and must leave both parts of the enclosing possession at least the decoder's minimum
length. A deletion needs p < 0.35 and hands the frames to the other team only when that team holds a neighbouring
possession, never between two stoppages. On BAR-ATH the verifier changes 0.17% of the frames in six stretches
(211 → 216 possessions).

## 4. Possession rules implemented

- A possession is a maximal run of one team with the ball alive. Dead ball is always D, never a possession.
- A change of possession needs controlled possession by the other team. This is encoded in the training labels
  (section 3.3) and in the decoder's switch penalty and soft minimum length.
- During loose or contested phases the decoder keeps the previous team unless the evidence for the other team
  persists.
- After a stoppage the possession is re-decided from the evidence of the first seconds of play (restart formation,
  who is on the ball).

## 5. Missing and noisy tracking

- The ball is missing on 41% of graded frames, mostly while it is dead. In play the gaps are short once filled from
  the broadcast ball. Missing values stay NaN; the gradient-boosted trees handle them natively, and the ball-free team
  features keep the classifier informed when the ball is lost.
- No player identities and slot swaps: every feature is collective (team level), never per slot.
- Noise in positions and in the ball: the classifier is trained on open tracking degraded the same way (section 3.3),
  and ±1 s logit smoothing plus the decoder's duration prior suppress flicker.
- The ATD fills some short ball gaps by prediction (over-smooth straight runs). Removing them was tested and not
  supported on external data, so they are kept.

## 6. Validation and model selection

Every idea was measured on held-out external matches with a fixed protocol:

- **DFL** leave-one-match-out (7 matches), labelled with a tracking-derived controlled-possession reading.
- **Metrica** leave-one-game-out (3 games × 3 degradations), controlled-possession labels from events.
- **SkillCorner** 20 A-League matches (broadcast tracking, never used for training), with two label conventions:
  phases of play and player possessions.

Each set is scored with the model's own dead-ball estimate and with the true dead ball. DFL is also scored with
controlled possession derived from its synchronised event data, which gives 10 contexts.
Decisions use the worst-case regret over the contexts. A difference below 0.005 keeps the simpler or current model.
Candidates are checked on at least 3 LightGBM seeds and with a paired match bootstrap. Stress tests use unseen
degradations (pre-smoothed tracking, ATD-like predicted ball runs).

The verifier (section 3.5) was judged in the same way: every match is scored by a verifier that never saw it
(leave-one-match-out over 30 matches, the three sources pooled), over three team-model seeds, both dead-ball channels
and two verifier seeds, with neighbouring thresholds as a check.

The BiGRU blend needed one more step. The shipped BiGRU checkpoints were trained on all seven DFL matches, so DFL
could not judge anything that uses them. The BiGRU was therefore retrained seven times with the same recipe, each time
without one DFL match (three seeds each, on a cloud GPU), and DFL is scored with these held-out probabilities, both in
the blend and in the verifier's margin. Each blend seed is paired with one team-model seed. With the held-out
probabilities two things came to light: the GRU alone is weaker than the classifier on DFL (frame accuracy 0.90–0.91
against 0.91), so the 0.75 weight chosen earlier without DFL lost there; and the previous submission (v13 = the
classifier + the verifier, trained with DFL rows lacking a BiGRU margin) scores 0.006–0.012 lower on DFL once its
verifier sees a held-out margin, as it does on BAR-ATH. The submission was chosen among the pre-registered weights,
with and without the verifier, against v13 scored that way.

The 5-minute public window (17 possessions) is used only to check that the pipeline is correct; its bootstrap
interval (0.44–0.83 spellF1) is far too wide to rank versions. One exception from the first day is stated openly: the
dead-ball rules of section 3.2 were developed while checking them against that window.

|---|---|---|---|

| Metrica (3 games) | 0.824 / 0.882 | 0.823 / 0.882 | 0.815 / 0.872 |
| SkillCorner, phases (20 matches) | 0.598 / 0.759 | 0.597 / 0.759 | 0.582 / 0.746 |
| SkillCorner, player possessions | 0.592 / 0.748 | 0.592 / 0.748 | 0.583 / 0.741 |

The submission (v14: the 0.5 blend + its verifier) against the previous submission (v13: the classifier + its
verifier, scored with a held-out BiGRU margin on DFL as it runs on BAR-ATH), mean of 3 team-model seeds × 2 verifier

| Context (own D / true D) | v13 | v14 | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFL, tracking-derived controlled | 0.764 / 0.792 | 0.770 / 0.794 | +0.006 [−0.002, +0.013] / +0.002 [−0.006, +0.009] |
| DFL, event-derived controlled | 0.777 / 0.803 | 0.785 / 0.809 | +0.008 [−0.002, +0.017] / +0.005 [−0.005, +0.015] |

Among v13 and the six blend variants (weights 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75, with and without the verifier) the worst-case regret
over the 10 contexts is 0.0165 for v13 and 0.0039 for v14, the lowest; a match bootstrap of the regret difference puts
it above the 0.005 margin in 94% of the draws. Scored as in round 15 (no BiGRU margin on DFL), v13 reaches
0.775 / 0.804 on DFL-tracking and v14 is 0.006 / 0.010 below it there, yet its worst-case regret is still the lowest
(0.0099 against 0.0165). Earlier, the verifier on top of the classifier alone (v13) had lowered the worst-case regret
from 0.019 (v10) to 0.004 within its own comparison.

- **Public window** (sanity check only, never used for selection): the file passes the official validator. The last
  reported check is v10's (v13 changes no frame there): spellF1 0.667 (bootstrap 0.44–0.83), macroF1 0.932, alive/dead
  F1 0.982, team accuracy on alive frames 0.953. The official smoothing baseline scores 0.326 there.
- **Full match** (no labels): 216 possessions (v13: 214, v10: 203), 118 dead-ball stretches, 50% dead time, home share
  of possession 0.61; v14 and v13 differ on 0.76% of the frames.

## 8. What did not work (selected)

Each of these is ≤ +0.003 or negative on the external protocol:

- decoder variants beyond the soft minimum length (restart-aware, time-varying switch costs, insertion and deletion
  scorers);
- sequence models on their own (a bidirectional GRU, temporal stacking); blended with the classifier, the shared
  BiGRU does help (section 3.3), but a 0.75 weight loses on DFL;
- a player-level controller model;
- role features;
- duel-outcome features and a contest specialist;
- ball-touch event features;
- adding the broadcast-tracked SkillCorner matches to training;
- self-training on the test match;
- ensembles;
- ball height (even the true height from the open data);
- moving decoded possession changes to the optimum of less-smoothed evidence (the lag of short possessions comes from
  the team model's feature windows as well as from the decoder);
- the rule "the restarting team did not touch the ball last" to recover possessions before a stoppage (it tells the
  last touch, not the last control);
- broadcast camera framing as possession evidence;
- player names in the commentary.

## 9. Limitations

- The remaining errors are short (< 4 s) in-play possessions after turnovers, especially duels and aerial balls, and
  their mirror image, spurious changes. Around those moments the tracking positions carry little more information
  than the model already uses; a simulation with perfect positions gains only about +0.005. The verifier recovers
  part of them, but its insertions are only weakly separable on DFL and Metrica (AUC about 0.7, with or without the
  BiGRU margin). What is missing is which team's player actually touched or controlled the ball, which would need
  reliable touch recognition from video.
- The BiGRU's weight is a compromise between the sets: on DFL, where the classifier is trained on the same kind of
  data, the GRU adds little; on SkillCorner, which neither model trained on, the blend gains most.
- Possession conventions differ between the training sets and the ground truth's provider, which is why model
  selection uses several conventions.
- The dead-ball rules use the broadcast recording; without it the model would rely on the learned dead-ball
  evidence only.

## 10. Reproducing the submission

```bash
# Python 3.12; pinned packages in requirements.txt
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe -r requirements.txt
git clone https://github.com/metrica-sports/more-than-a-hack-2027 external/more-than-a-hack-2027
# match bundle -> data/{tactical,broadcast} (or set MTAH_DATA_DIR)
python src/make_submission.py               # -> submissions/candidate_v14.csv
python external/more-than-a-hack-2027/evaluation/validate_submission.py submissions/candidate_v14.csv

# optional: retrain the team classifier from the open data (rewrites models/v10_team.txt)
python src/download_idsse.py                # open DFL / IDSSE data, CC BY 4.0, ~2.6 GB
python src/metrica_sample.py download       # Metrica sample games, pinned commit, ~185 MB
MTAH_RETRAIN=1 python src/make_submission.py
```

- **Default run.** The team classifier is shipped as `models/v10_team.txt` (2.9 MB, trained only on the open data),
  the verifier as `models/short_verifier_ins_g_blend50.txt` and `models/short_verifier_del_g_blend50.txt`, and the
  shared BiGRU as `models/bigru_dfl_pff_v1/`. The default run therefore needs only the provided data and the official
  repository (for the scorer and the public window). On the first run it also rebuilds the BiGRU's BAR-ATH
  probabilities on the CPU (`src/reproduce_shared_bigru.py`, a few minutes; it checks the result against the
  checkpoints' manifest). `--model model_v13` still writes the previous submission.
- **Retraining.** `MTAH_RETRAIN=1` rebuilds the simulated training inputs, the features and the team classifier from
  the open data in about 7 minutes on 24 cores; the submission is unchanged. The verifier classifiers come from the
  research pipeline (`src/exp_verify.py`, held-out team-model and BiGRU probabilities on the external sets; on DFL the
  leave-one-match-out BiGRU of `src/exp_bigru_lomo.py`, trained on a GPU with the PFF data) and are retrained byte for
  byte with `MTAH_RETRAIN_VERIFIER=1` when those caches exist.
- **Checks on Windows, Python 3.12.13, from an empty cache:**
  - the retrained model file is byte-identical to the shipped one;
  - both runs write the same submission (MD5 above).
- **Determinism.** Simulation seeds are fixed, LightGBM runs in deterministic mode with a fixed seed and thread count,
  and no GPU is used. LightGBM's deterministic mode is guaranteed for a fixed platform and thread count; on another
  platform a retrain could differ in the last bits, which is one more reason the trained classifier is shipped.
- **Line endings.** LightGBM 4.7 cannot read a model file with CRLF line endings, which a Windows checkout with Git's
  default `core.autocrlf=true` writes for text files. `.gitattributes` keeps `models/*.txt` byte for byte, and the
  pipeline reads the models as text (`src/bench.py`, `load_booster`), so a converted copy loads the same model.
- All intermediate files go to `cache/` (gitignored).

## 11. Data, licences and policy

- No match data and nothing derived from it at frame level is in the repository. `data/`, `cache/` and
  `submissions/` are gitignored.
- Open data is downloaded from its sources and not redistributed:
  - IDSSE / DFL (CC BY 4.0, Bassek et al. 2025, figshare 28196177);
  - Metrica Sports sample data (credited as requested by its README);
  - SkillCorner open data (MIT);
  - PFF FC / Gradient Sports FIFA World Cup 2022 data, obtained through the provider's access form and used by a team
    member to train the shared BiGRU checkpoints (the checkpoints contain no match data), and by us to train the
    leave-one-DFL-match-out copies used for validation and for the verifier's DFL margins (not shipped).
- The labels are produced entirely by the algorithm; no frame was annotated by hand.
